# `modflow_plume`

Where a DISSOLVED RELEASE goes in an unconfined aquifer - a conservative solute plume over time, checked against measured wells.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| module | `gwf` - 508 keywords in its dictionary, of which this template states 13 |
| solves | `trid3nt_server.workflows.modflow.engine.solve_case` |
| engine defaults | every keyword this template does not state keeps the engine's own default; `describe_keywords` names it with that default, and `keywords={...}` sets it |

## The data it consumes

| row | produced by | what it is | datum |
|---|---|---|---|
| `domain` | matched on a need for hydrography | the closed polygon this run solves over, as a uri, a layer name or a drawn shape; unfilled, the run matches a source of hydrography. | - |
| `source` | supplied by the caller | The polygon the effluent infiltrates over, as a drawn shape or a layer: the beds of the release. The run places the source on the cells whose centres it holds. | - |
| `bed` | matched on a need for terrain | The land surface: the terrain the mesh paints, which the aquifer's top is and the streams drain at. A DEM, or a depth in metres below the model's zero for a flat surface. | - |
| `saturated_thickness` | matched on a need for aquifer property | How thick the saturated aquifer is, its base that far below the water table: a number in metres, or a raster publishing its unit; unfilled, the source publishing aquifer_saturated_thickness here. | - |
| `transmissivity` | matched on a need for aquifer property | The aquifer's transmissivity: a number in square metres per day, or a raster publishing its unit; unfilled, the source publishing aquifer_transmissivity here. | - |
| `water_table_depth` | matched on a need for groundwater level | How far below the land surface the water table stands before the solve: a number in metres, or a raster publishing its unit; unfilled, the source publishing water_table_depth here. | - |
| `recharge` | matched on a need for aquifer property | What reaches the water table over the domain: a number in metres per day, or a raster publishing its unit; unfilled, the source publishing groundwater_recharge here. | - |
| `streams` | matched on a need for hydrography | the hydrography this run reads, as a uri or a layer name; unfilled, the run matches a source of hydrography. | - |
| `observe` | matched on a need for water quality sample | The measured concentrations of the solute at wells, at the snapshot: every well reporting it, each compared with the model at its own cell; unfilled, the measured water quality here. | - |
| `mesh` | supplied by the caller | a mesh this case already built, as its uri or its layer name, solved on in place of the one the run would build; the user may state one; unstated, the run builds its own. | - |

## The inputs

The values the template declares. `desc` is what the model reads when it fills one.

| input | units | default | desc |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drain_conductance` | m2/day | required | The conductance of the stream beds the aquifer drains through, per cell a stream crosses: how readily water at a head above the bed leaves the aquifer. No dataset measures it, so it is stated |
| `source_rate` | m/day | required | The depth of treated effluent that infiltrates per day over the source polygon, spread over the polygon as drawn: the release's total volume over its period divided by the polygon's area. It enters the flow as recharge on top of the natural recharge, and it is stated |
| `source_concentration` | - | required | The concentration of the solute in the effluent that infiltrates, in concentration_units. The infiltrating water carries it into the transport model, and it is stated |
| `background_concentration` | - | required | The concentration of the solute in the aquifer's own water before the release, which is also that of the natural recharge replacing it, in concentration_units. It is stated |
| `porosity` | - | required | The effective porosity the solute moves through, a fraction of the aquifer's volume (dimensionless). It is stated |
| `longitudinal_dispersivity` | m | required | The dispersivity of the solute along the flow, at the scale of the plume (m). It is stated |
| `transverse_dispersivity` | m | required | The horizontal dispersivity of the solute across the flow, at the scale of the plume (m). It is stated |
| `snapshot` | - | required | The moment the measured concentrations are read at and compared with the model's: an ISO date or datetime (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). The run itself starts at event_time, and the period it marches must reach this moment |
| `solute` | - | required | What the plume carries, in the measuring source's own word for it (a Water Quality Portal CharacteristicName, such as 'Boron'). The measured wells are asked for that word |
| `mesh_resolution_m` | m | optional | Target element edge or cell length the mesh is built at. The granularity is the USER's and nothing refuses one: absent, the mesh resolves the finest data it stands on, and the card states the node count it comes to |
| `event_time` | - | optional | The moment the scenario is read at - an ISO date or datetime (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ), from phrasing like 'during last Tuesday's storm'. Each source keeps its own retention, and a request deeper than one refuses typed |
| `vertical_frame` | - | NAVD88 | Vertical datum the bed's elevations are counted from, and with them the level over it. A source published on another frame reaches this one through a measured offset, and a pair nobody publishes an offset between refuses by name |
| `concentration_units` | - | required | The unit every concentration this run carries is counted in - the unit its source and starting concentrations are stated in, such as mg/L. A measured concentration is converted into it, and a reading no conversion reaches refuses |
